affected_components.role: The verifier iterates over the provided commitments to construct the Feldman right-hand side and has no shown t+1 length check.

code_slices.fixed: The report states PR #2007 checks commitment length when commitments are initially received in FROST DKG round 1; no patch diff is present.
code_slices.surrounding_context: Before the commitment loop, Verify obtains the curve from the first commitment and validates the share against that curve.
code_slices.vulnerable: The report-embedded Verify method initializes rhs from Commitments[0], loops from j=1 to len(Commitments)-1, adds each commitment multiplied by a successive power of share.Id, and returns nil if lhs.Equal(rhs).

negative_controls: Reject a vector whose cardinality differs from t+1 at initial FROST DKG round-1 receipt.
No supplied artifact demonstrates execution of either outcome for an oversized vector.
observability.positive_marker: The report-embedded code returns nil only if the group-element equality check succeeds after folding all supplied commitments.

impact.affected_asset: The threshold-DKG polynomial-degree structure and resulting distributed-key-generation trust assumptions.
impact.attacker_capability: A malicious DKG participant can submit a commitment vector larger than t+1.
impact.security_effect: FROST DKG correctness and security-proof assumptions can be undermined by a commitment representation outside the required degree bound.

causal_trace.summary: A DKG participant can provide a commitment vector with more than t+1 entries, while the protocol expects commitments for a degree-t polynomial.
The verifier does not enforce that the commitment-vector cardinality equals t+1, the coefficient count for the required degree-t polynomial.

FeldmanVerifier.Verify derives its right-hand group element by iterating through every supplied commitment and successive powers of the share identifier, then accepts when the computed left and right group elements are equal.
Oversized commitments permit an increased polynomial length outside the assumed threshold-DKG structure, undermining the FROST DKG assumption and the applicability of its academic security proofs.

failure.operation: Fold every received commitment into the Feldman verification equation without enforcing the degree-derived commitment count.

primary_invariant.statement: For FROST DKG with a degree-t polynomial, a received commitment vector must contain exactly t+1 commitments.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The embedded FeldmanVerifier.Verify implementation indexes and folds all entries in Commitments but performs no cardinality comparison against t+1 before its equality-based acceptance decision.

quality.review_notes: The public audit report contains the finding, report-embedded verifier code, recommendation, and a stated PR #2007 resolution, but the bundle has no patch diff, exact upstream kryptology revision, malformed-vector test, or runtime trace. The record therefore bounds impact to violation of FROST DKG assumptions/security-proof coverage and does not infer key extraction, signature forgery, or validator compromise.

remediation.invariant_restored: Commitments initially received in FROST DKG round 1 are constrained to exactly t+1 entries for the degree-t polynomial.
mitigation_classes: enforce degree-derived commitment cardinality at DKG message receipt
reject commitment vectors whose length differs from t+1
